sec: Viral replication steps with drug classes, and acute HIV infection

items.q: Viral entry — match the step to its event — 1) First attachment 2) Co-receptor binding 3) Post-binding change 4) Final step … A) Conformational change in gp41 B) Conformational change in gp120 C) CXCR4 on lymphocytes, CCR5 on macrophages D) Fusion and uncoating of the virus
items.exp: 'Step-1 : Viral entry : Conformational change in gp120; b. Co-receptor binding (CXCR4 - lymphocyte, CCR5 - macrophages); Conformational change in gp41; C. Fusion uncoating of virus'. (Book p1064)

items.q: Co-receptors — match — 1) CXCR4 2) CCR5 … A) Macrophages B) Lymphocytes

Drug classes matched to the replication step — match — 1) Entry 2) Fusion 3) Integration 4) Release … A) Fusion inhibitor given subcutaneously B) Protease inhibitors C) Integrase inhibitors given orally D) Co-receptor blocker given orally
items.exp: 'Co-receptor blocker (oral)' at entry, 'Fusion inhibitor (s/c)', 'Integrase inhibitors (Oral)' at integration and 'Cleaved by protease … Protease inhibitors' at release. (Book p1064)

items.q: Which step converts viral RNA into DNA in the printed cycle?
items.exp: 'Viral RNA → DNA' is the step after viral entry and before integration. (Book p1064)

items.q: What makes the released virion mature, according to the page?
items.exp: 'Cleaved by protease → mature virus released'. (Book p1064)

items.q: Fill up: 'Primary infection → incubation period (______ weeks) → acute infectious syndrome / acute HIV infection.'
What illness does the page print that acute HIV infection mimics?
Acute HIV syndrome — match the symptom group — 1) Constitutional 2) Throat 3) Nodes 4) Gut and skin … A) Sore throat B) Fever C) Lymphadenopathy D) Diarrhoea and rash
items.exp: 'Clinical Symptoms : Fever, Sore throat, Lymphadenopathy, · Diarrhea, · Rash'. (Book p1064)

items.q: What proportion of acute HIV infections resolve symptomatically, and what proportion are fulminant?
items.exp: '> 90% : Symptoms resolve'; '≥10% : Fulminant stage (meningoencephalitis)'. (Both figures are printed as given.) (Book p1064)

items.q: Which form does the fulminant stage take, as printed?

Judge the acute-HIV block: I Opportunistic infections are absent in acute HIV infection. II After the acute illness the virus is established in GALT with long subclinical replication (clinical latency).
items.exp: 'No opportunistic infections', 'Establishment of infection in GALT' and 'Subclinical replication for long period (clinical latency)'. (Book p1064)

items.q: Where is infection established during the long subclinical period?
